blocks.x: Well Kenny, really, in a way, I mean the development itself, I mean on the horns and everything else -- I mean what it turned out to be in the end was that everybody gained the facility to speed up.
Uh-huh.
I mean the instrumentalists, I mean, gained, like the years that Dizzy worked at it, and Charlie.
Right.
The use of the chords gained so much familiarity with them that they could move that much faster.
Right, absolutely.
And you're doing the same thing in the rhythm.
Right.
So that the whole thing can move ahead that much faster.
That's right.
So there it is, you know, like you see the advance in the field.

Move together simultaneously. Everything is sort of moving toward this same -- the same goal, but one is moving one way and another, you know, carrying the harmony, and another is moving in the rhythm, and another one is moving
in the bass and things like that.
Yeah.
But they're all moving in the same goal. They have the same boot in mind.
Yeah.
.I think --

Well, I guess that for Diz and Bird were -- had their thing, and working it out, you know, from the melodic point of view. The rhythmic and melodic combined. But you were working out the rhythm end of it.
That's right, and it seemed to all fit in together.
Yeah. Well, you all inspired each other.
Yeah. I think that's what it was.
Yeah.
We were all working toward the same end, but a distance, miles apart, you know.
Yeah.
And then all that had to be done was for it to be -- bring it together, you know?
Yeah. Yeah.
And when it came together everybody said, 'Wow. Gee whiz, that's it.'
Yeah.
